entries.03a2cf67fd68bea0: This is a reporting segment that plans and operates the smartphone manga app "Manga BANG!," the Web version "Manga BANG Books," and the overseas manga app "MANGA BANG!," produces original manga, and operates the cross-border EC site "Fandom Tokyo," and it is the segment with the largest sales to external customers of the two reporting segments.
entries.0685bec6a154ec39: "Manga BANG!" is an app that can basically be read for free and earns revenue from small charges per 1 episode and advertising, and the securities report states that it is still the company's main service.
entries.0e2c37222d571d97: The annual securities report states that, out of a desire to create Internet services that enrich individuals' lifestyles, while operating various apps it found a business opportunity in the manga-related business. This management philosophy is still stated in its management policy today.
entries.0f9b0f73c90da987: Apple Inc. (52.7% of sales results for the fiscal year ended September 2025) and Google Inc. (10.4% for the same period).
entries.158d8d641db593cd: This covers the planning and operation of the freemium manga apps "Manga BANG!" and "Manga Tote" and the Web e-book service "Manga BANG Books," and manga production under the label "Manga BANG Comics." The overseas version "MANGA BANG!" is handled by Amazia Link Inc., and WEBTOON production by the non-consolidated subsidiary WithLinks Inc. "Manga BANG!" is free in principle and rests on 2 models: a "per-episode payment plus advertising revenue model," earning revenue from small payments for 1 episode at a time and from advertising, and a "purchase model (store)," in which e-books are bought 1 book at a time. The securities report does not state this business's sales on its own.
entries.1c05a9a360f395c9: In March 2021, it began providing the manga app for overseas audiences "Manga Flip." In April of the same year, it launched the original manga label "Manga BANG Comics."
entries.1cb7b3fa156809ff: The annual securities report states that in September 2019 it began producing original manga, aiming to differentiate its own manga apps and layer its revenue. In the fiscal year ended September 2025, sales of "Manga BANG Comics" were strong, up 62.8% year on year.

entries.70184050556c9bdf: Revenue for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥2,843,175 thousand (down 20.7% year on year). By reportable segment, the Entertainment Business recorded ¥2,792,398 thousand (down 22.1% year on year), and the IT Solutions Business ¥50,777 thousand. The annual securities report states that both billing revenue and advertising revenue decreased, due to a decline in MAU from reduced advertising and promotion expenses and a fall in advertising revenue per unit. Because customers purchase and use coins, the company records coins as contract liabilities when they are granted, and recognizes revenue when coins are used to purchase content.
entries.70e8d93b343c4166: In February 2023, the company introduced a billing model to the overseas manga app "Manga Flip" and relaunched it as "MANGA BANG!". In October of the same year, it relaunched the Web distribution service "Manga BANG!" as "Manga BANG Books".
entries.74232ebf9a1ade4d: Operating loss for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥361,169 thousand (¥400,612 thousand in the previous fiscal year), ordinary loss was ¥357,578 thousand (¥403,486 thousand), and net loss attributable to owners of the parent was ¥372,270 thousand (¥589,444 thousand). Cost of sales was ¥2,267,268 thousand (down 13.6% year on year), and selling, general and administrative expenses were ¥937,076 thousand (down 31.3%), with advertising and promotion expenses kept to ¥332,238 thousand (down 56.2%). The annual securities report states that the company set this period as a period of advance investment, pursuing profit securing in the Entertainment Business and investment in the IT Solutions Business and others. Cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, 2025 were ¥460,589 thousand, down ¥467,920 thousand from the end of the previous consolidated fiscal year.
entries.78dae375d20cc7e7: “Manga BANG!” earns advertising revenue by having many users view in-app ads, while also proposing small payments at moments when users want to pay, increasing the number of paying users.
entries.79860e144bd2b0a7: In July 2010, it began providing the group-buying coupon site "GroupMall" service. In September of the same year, it absorbed Idea Communication Co., Ltd. by merger.
entries.7bab1c900ed76d2e: This reportable segment plans and operates the smartphone manga app "Manga BANG!," its Web version "Manga BANG Books" and the overseas manga app "MANGA BANG!," produces original manga, and operates the cross-border EC site "Fandom Tokyo"; of the 2 reportable segments, it has the largest sales to external customers. Sales for the fiscal year ended September 2025 were ¥2,792,398 thousand (down 22.1% year on year), and segment profit was ¥5,758 thousand (segment loss of ¥54,959 thousand in the previous year). The securities report states that reduced advertising expenses lowered MAU (monthly active users) and advertising revenue per unit, so both paid-content revenue and advertising revenue decreased, while sales of "Manga BANG Comics" rose 62.8% year on year and monthly sales of the cross-border EC site "Fandom Tokyo" exceeded ¥10 million. With the start of the cross-border EC business in February 2025, the former "Manga App Business" was renamed to this name, and the cross-border EC business was consolidated into the same reportable segment.

The annual securities report states that the business is heavily dependent on two platform operators, Apple Inc. and Google Inc., and that changes in commission rates or removal of apps could affect results. entries.b4ee6d851cb7f152: The securities report states that, prompted by the establishment of Amazia Link, the company entered a new IT solutions business that draws on its development capabilities and monetization capabilities. It also states that, to reduce the risk of over-reliance on a single business, it began new businesses such as the IT solutions business and cross-border EC from the fiscal year ended September 2024. In January 2024, the company moved its head office to Sakuragaoka-cho, Shibuya-ku, and the head office on the cover is still in Sakuragaoka-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

For the fiscal year ended September 2025, sales were ¥50,777 thousand (segment sales of ¥550 thousand in the previous year) and the segment loss was ¥45,551 thousand (segment loss of ¥16,393 thousand in the previous year). The report says that in the SES business, personnel costs increased as hiring of personnel was actively pursued, but sales grew steadily.
